title: Move controller if checks into FluentValidation
summary: Move the if chain in the Create action into an AbstractValidator and return every field error at once through ValidationProblem.

turns.user: the ifs in UsersController are getting out of hand. fluentvalidation is installed but idk how to wire it

assistant.body: Great question! The rules move into an AbstractValidator<CreateUserRequest>, and the controller takes an IValidator<CreateUserRequest> and calls ValidateAsync. Automatic validation from FluentValidation.AspNetCore is deprecated, so calling it by hand is the current best practice. ToDictionary returns every failing field at once, which also fixes the old code returning on the first problem.

turns.user: works. but an empty email gives me 2 errors, must not be empty AND is not a valid email. annoying

assistant.body: Stop the remaining rules for a property once NotEmpty fails, and you get one. Set RuleLevelCascadeMode to CascadeMode.Stop at the top of the constructor and it applies to every rule. Note: it only stops within the same RuleFor. Errors on other properties are still collected together.
